newsitem.title: UK: EMIRATES AIMS FOR 12-15 PCT MORE UK CARGO IN 97-98.
newsitem.headline: EMIRATES AIMS FOR 12-15 PCT MORE UK CARGO IN 97-98.

text.p: Emirates has forecast it will carry 12 to 15 percent more UK inbound and outbound cargo in the year to end-March 1998 than the 17,000 tonnes it flew in 1996-97, said its UK/Ireland cargo manager Ray Dissan.

The 17,000 tonnes total was up 21 percent on 1995/96, mainly as a result of introducing Boeing 777 aircraft on the route in July 1996, supplementing Airbus A310s and A300s and raising the carrier's UK-Dubai capacity by 45 percent.
"We will not be getting any further capacity this year and so therefore our tonnage gowth will be restricted to 12-15 percent," Dissan told Reuters.
He also said that the Dubai government-owned airline increased its cargo traffic to and from Ireland by 65 percent in 1996/97 to 980 tonnes.

"This was mainly the result of winning a major new computer cargo contract. But as a similar new contract is unlikely this year, and bearing in mind fierce competition in the Irish market being provided by the likes of Singapore Airlines and KLM, my target for Ireland is to achieve a 10 percent tonnage increase for 1997-98," he said. - Reuters Air Cargo Service, Tel+44 171 5427706 Fax+5017 - www.racs.com
